pageCache.text:
Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to our brilliant, dynamic Academy, sponsored by both the Church of England and the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. Since becoming Principal in September 2020, I have ensured that all our students continue to flourish and excel through strong educational provision and unparalleled pastoral care. Our results this summer at both A Level and GCSE are testimony to a real focus on excellent teaching and learning and on preparing our students to be successful in their next steps.
Our Vision
‘Learning together to flourish’, is lived out every day; a vision informed by our Christian values. We believe in educating the whole child and our Christian values of joy, perseverance, servant leadership, charity and forgiveness underpin everything we stand for.
Discover
If you are new to the Academy, you may want to explore this section and find out what makes us unique.
News
Find out what's been going on around the Academy via our Blog and CA Updates (Newsletters).
Anchor and Flourish newsletter
Download the latest Academy newsletter here or subscribe to our mailing list and receive them directly to your inbox.

Having opened in September 2009 we are now an established, successful and oversubscribed academy. Every year over several hundred students want to join us in Year 7. Our outstanding and competitive Sixth Form also attracts hundreds of external applicants each year.
As a parent of three girls and an educator with thirty years of experience behind me, I am passionate and committed about the difference school can make to our children.
Our Academy vision: ‘Learning together to flourish’, is lived out every day and is a vision genuinely informed by our Christian values. These values of forgiveness, joy, perseverance, charity and servant leadership are an integral part of our journey to success. Visitors always comment on the sense of purpose; of belonging and of our commitment to diversity and inclusion.
Our mission: Work Hard Be Kind No Excuses, provides students with a compass to guide and direct their own journey. And our Chelsea Academy Way for Behaviour clearly sets out our expectations, so that every student understands how they should conduct themselves both in and out of school.
We have a longer school day than most other local schools. Each day (apart from Wednesday) is made up of six, 55 minute lessons. Our curriculum is broad in Year 7, 8 and 9. This allows students to discover and master subjects such as Citizenship, the Arts and languages. These are of course in addition to the core building block subjects of English, Maths and Science. Towards the end of Year 9 students choose their GCSE options for the two year GCSE programme which starts in Year 10. All students take GCSE RE at the end of Year 10; the results are incredible and empower our young people as they then move into Year 11 and complete the rest of their GCSEs. Our Sixth Form offer is unique as we specialise in A Level only programmes and in addition have chosen to offer A Levels such as Design & Technology and English Literature & Language that are not offered locally. The Sixth Form is housed in a stunning new space on the ground floor which through the layout, furniture and staffing helps students transition from Year 11, work independently and take advantage of the many opportunities we offer. These include the weekly lecture series and superb Higher Education and Careers guidance.
Our Extended Curriculum ensures that students benefit from having a rich ‘all round’ experience. Over 50 free after-school clubs operate every week. We are fortunate that the Chelsea Academy Foundation funds and supports much of our Extended Curriculum offer. We recognise that many busy working parents are looking for a school that provides wrap-around care for younger Key Stage 3 students and so we open at 8am providing breakfast and after school clubs run until at least 4.30pm.
As a result of our Academy offer, by the time students leave at either 16 or 18, they will have achieved a strong set of qualifications but also will have developed the resilience, wisdom, hope and skills with which to lead happy, healthy and fulfilling lives.
This website holds a range of information whether you are a prospective parent or carer, an aspiring student, a would-be member of staff or anyone interested in the Academy. The news section of the website is regularly updated with what we have been up to. Please take a look. Parents and carers, do visit the Parent Portal, which has content specifically for you. If you are interested in joining us as a member of staff, then the careers section has what you need. Current students and staff can access emails, calendars and Google drive through the Chelsea Academy Learning Cloud (CALC).
I am exceptionally proud and privileged to lead Chelsea Academy. It is a wonderful and fast moving environment. We benefit from being in a fantastic London location and from the opportunity to take advantage of excellent partnerships, both local and further afield. The Academy is also fortunate to have an outstanding Board of governors. They are truly invested and interested in the Academy.
Please feel free to arrange a visit to the Academy or to contact us for further information. If you are intending to visit and find out more about the Academy for your Y5 or 6 child, please do visit our Admissions page, where you should find all the information you need. Our Registrar, Jane Livesey is also happy to speak to you for an informal chat.
Mariella Ardron
Principal, Chelsea Academy

pageCache.pageTitle: London Diocesan Board for Schools annual Church Service - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
On Thursday, our Chaplain Anita, along with Mrs Holgate and Laura Malkin our governor, escorted students who regularly visit to chapel to the annual schools’ church service at St Paul’s Cathedral.
The theme of the service was “The Power of Forgiveness: Restoring Friendship”, and we heard readings and music performed by over 370 school children from across the Diocese of London. Chelsea Academy is one of the newest of the 152 schools in the London Diocesan Board for Schools. To celebrate the bringing together of all these different schools, we were sent a jigsaw piece to decorate, which was then put together with all the other jigsaw pieces in the cathedral.
We had a joyful afternoon full of music and celebration, even though it was grey and gloomy outside.

pageCache.pageTitle: CHELSEA ACADEMY CELEBRATES OUTSTANDING 2026 A LEVEL RESULTS AND TOP UNIVERSITY DESTINATIONS - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
Students and staff at Chelsea Academy were celebrating last Thursday following the publication of the 2026 provisional A Level results, which highlight sustained academic growth and impressive individual achievements.
This year’s results reflect a sustained upward trajectory. Students at the Academy achieved an average grade of a high B-, with an Average Point Score (APS) of 34.89. This represents a significant 2.32-point increase compared to 2023/2024 whilst maintaining consistently strong outcomes across all subject areas.
Demonstrating high academic ambition, a fifth of all grades awarded were A* or A (20.1%), while an impressive 54% were graded A* to B, matching the Academy’s high watermark from the previous academic year. Early benchmark data indicates that official value-added measures, scheduled for publication in early 2027, will firmly align with last year’s strong progress figures.
The cohort’s performance has secured individual places at a range of highly aspirational and selective higher education institutions, including Imperial College London, UCL, King’s College London, University of Warwick, University of Bath, University of Exeter and City St George’s.
Highlights of individual university destinations include:
Imperial College London:
Computing (A*A*AA) and Electrical & Electronic Engineering (A*AAA)
Astrophysics (A*A*AA), Mathematics (A*A*B), and International Management (AAA)
King’s College London:
Dentistry (A*A*A) and Business Management (A*AA)
University of Warwick:
Politics & International Studies (A*AA) and Law with French (A*AB & AAB)
City St George’s, University of London:
University of Exeter:
Academy leaders praised students for their determination and dedication. “I am immensely proud of our Year 13 students”; Mariella Ardron, Principal at Chelsea Academy. “These results are a clear reflection of their ambition, resilience, and incredible work ethic over the past two years. To see so many of our young people securing places at world leading universities – studying everything from Dentistry and Astrophysics to Law and Nursing – is fantastic. They have shown what can be achieved when our Academy community works together to flourish, and I wish them every success as they take their next steps.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Much Ado About Something - Year 10’s Journey to The Globe! - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text: Shakespeare’s Globe held as much wonder for our Year 10 group as it did for Londoners in 1599. Luckily, we had glorious sunshine for our visit to watch Much Ado About Nothing on Thursday. This wonderfully directed, engaging production was full of exquisite animal masks (Adeena, with her sharp analytical eye, noted how each animal reflected the personality of the character wearing it), dancing and tons of comical moments that had us all laughing and clapping along. Just like in the sixteenth century, the busy theatre buzzed with excited chatter, the same hustle and bustle as for an original audience. We watched the show with many other school groups, which created a real sense of community in the central yard and galleries. It was so much fun to look around and see so many happy faces, not least Chelsea Academy’s!

pageCache.pageTitle: Come and Work With Us - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
Vacancies at Chelsea Academy
Please click on the box below for our current vacancies which are hosted by TES. All vacancies require the submission of a TES digital application form. We do not accept CVs. To find out more about Chelsea Academy please visit our school portal on TES.
Training Opportunities
As a training school we work with a range of training providers such as King’s College London, the Institute of Education, WLTTA and Teach First. Should you require further information please contact Louise Dack at admin@chelsea-academy.org
Working at Chelsea Academy
Chelsea Academy is a fantastic and unique place to work. Staff turnover is low and many staff have worked their way up to middle and senior leadership while at the Academy. Staff have access to first class facilities; motivated and committed students, all within an ethos of bespoke professional development and self improvement.
We are situated in a stunning contemporary site, adjacent to Chelsea Harbour. We are easily accessible by overground, tube, bus or even boat! Whether you join as an associate member of staff, an ECT, middle leader or a member of the Leadership Team; your development is of paramount importance to us. We are committed to ensuring that all staff have access to outstanding CPD, be this at the Academy through our in-house programmes; through accredited providers of reformed NPQ programmes, or through other bespoke opportunities including peer reviews, supporting other schools. We also have an innovative approach to staff development when the Academy closes early for two hours every Wednesday, enabling us to offer the most up to date training and development.
Staff are the Academy’s greatest resource and we want to invest in you! We are always looking for excellent and ambitious teachers to join us and are committed to ensuring your wellbeing is a priority. We ensure that your workload is manageable and the camaraderie and support of your colleagues enables you to feel very much part of the Chelsea Academy family. Every member of teaching staff can have a late start or early departure one day a week and we have a discrete marking day in January in acknowledgement of staff wellbeing. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package including:
Supportive of flexible working
Private health insurance including physiotherapy
Free lunch
An Academy laptop
Dynamic pay progression Significant PPA time
Equal Opportunities
Chelsea Academy is an inclusive employer. We welcome applications from suitable candidates no matter their gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, or disability however, we do expect all our staff to note and follow our Christian ethos which is outlined on our website.
Safeguarding
Chelsea Academy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All successful applicants will have to be able to satisfy an enhanced disclosure check with the Disclosure and Barring Service.

pageCache.pageTitle: Inspirational art trip to the Tate Modern  - Thanks to our Jack Petchey Award winner! - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
Mr Doubble, Miss Troddan and Year 9 Art students would like to extend a massive thank you to our recent Jack Petchey Award winner.
Our winner kindly chose to spend their well earned grant money on funding a trip to the Tate Modern. The Year 9s spent a fascinating day exploring the galleries, making it a really positive and informative experience for everyone involved.

pageCache.pageTitle: Adventure Unleashed: Year 8 Conquers the Coast - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
Year 8 traded the classroom for the coast on an unforgettable Land & Wave expedition to Bournemouth. The trip was an electric blend of adventure and teamwork, centered around building resilience through shared challenges.
On the water, students navigated Swanage Bay with jumbo paddleboarding and kayaking. Whether they were coordinating paddles in chaotic harmony or balancing through the surf, the focus remained on mutual encouragement and building confidence on the waves.
The action continued on land with archery and climbing, where precision and grit were put to the test. Near Corfe Castle, the group mastered bushcraft skills, engineering waterproof shelters and perfecting fire-lighting techniques to survive the elements.
Evenings were spent sharing stories and celebrating the day’s victories. From hitting a bullseye to scaling new heights, Year 8 showed incredible spirit and determination. Well done on creating a fantastic core memory!

pageCache.pageTitle: Artistic Excellence: Mariem Exhibits with the Painter-Stainers’ Company - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text: It is with great pride that we recognise Mariem (Year 10) for her selection in the Painter-Stainers’ Schools Prize, held on Friday, 17th April. The Painter-Stainers’ Company is a venerable institution among the City of London Guilds, and Mariem’s inclusion in the exhibition is a significant feat. The ceremony was further distinguished by the presence of the Lord Mayor of London, who presided over the prize-giving.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 12 Fieldwork Success at Juniper Hall  - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
The Year 12 A-Level Biologists visited Juniper Hall FSC Centre in Dorking, Surrey, completing environmental and ecological investigations for their Practical Endorsement with the centre’s tutors.
Day 1 began with a capture-mark-recapture technique on pond snails using “snailpaint” to estimate population size. Next, they hiked to the woodlands to compare biodiversity in coppiced versus mature areas using systematic quadrat sampling and light meters, followed by data analysis back in the lab. They then collected woodlice for a choice chamber investigation on abiotic preferences, running another statistical test. After a delicious dinner, students learned to set mammal traps, camouflaging them from local foxes before leaving them overnight. Before bed, everyone enjoyed a campfire with marshmallow s’mores, hot chocolate, and games in the evening sun.
Day 2 started with the exciting opening of the traps, revealing six small rodents (wood mice and voles!). They then hiked to the base of Box Hill, taking in stunning views of the Surrey Hills while using line transects to analyze changes in plant species richness and evenness. The final study involved recapturing the pond snails to complete their mathematical analysis.
They boarded the coach home totally exhausted, but thrilled with a wonderful countryside experience full of great laughs and memories!

Work Hard

Be Kind
Love is patient; love is kind; love is not envious or boastful or arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice in wrongdoing, but rejoices in the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
No Excuses
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.
Our Christian ethos is at the core of our mission and our identified Christian values.
This phrase: ‘Anchored in Christ’ is used prominently throughout the Academy branding; our school badge is an anchor for this very reason. The anchor divides the badge into five distinct areas, which themselves represent our five chosen values. The Academy’s five identified prominent Christian values – Forgiveness, Joy, Perseverance, Charity and Servant Leadership – reflect the character of Christ’s love. Our values underpin daily life at the Academy and inform all that we do to make the Academy such a unique, diverse and flourishing place. Our Behaviour Curriculum has our ethos, values and mission at its heart. We are fortunate to have a Chaplain who provides dynamic ministry to students and staff; helping all in our community to grow spiritually and know the love of God. They work with local clergy to look both inwards and outwards.
Whilst we proudly celebrate our status as a Church of England academy we welcome students of all or no faiths. We are all united in our vision that Learning together we flourish whatever our beliefs or background. In November 2024 we achieved the SIAMS Judgement 1. Over the last four years the Academy has hosted gala charity dinners, staff training sessions, conferences, dance performances, sports events and summer holiday schemes. The versatile space means that we can host a number of different events at the same time. Availability of all spaces is limited to evenings, weekends and school holidays. The spaces for hire include a large sports hall, activities hall, two MUGAs (football pitches), a theatre and a conference room. All facilities are maintained to the highest standards and offer an attractive alternative to expensive conference centres.
Our hire rates are very competitive and we are easily accessible from central London and major transport hubs.
For more information please email lettings@chelsea-academy.org.
Sports Hall
We have a large sports hall (33m x 18m) which can be split into two separate rooms using nets which stretch the width of the room.
This space is ideal for basketball and five-a-side football.
Activities Hall
The activities hall (8m x 9m) can be used for a variety of different classes and activities, including dance and exercise.
It has a mirrored wall with a ballet bar, as well as an impressive climbing wall.
Multi-use Games Areas
The Academy is home to two impressive Multi Use Games Areas (MUGAs) that are available for hire for a number of sporting activities, including football matches.
The MUGAs are situated on the first floor roof, and are surrounded by a caged fence. The larger MUGA is full size and has match point two all-weather surfacing.
Conference Room
Our conference room (8.7m by 7.9m) is on the first floor and has lots of natural light. It seats 20 boardroom style and 25 classroom style.
It is fully equipped with data projector, interactive smartboard and flip chart.
Theatre
We have an impressive theatre (16m by 9m) that can seat up to 340 people.
It boasts retractable seating, as well as a balcony viewing area. It can be set out in various different conference styles including cabaret, meeting and dining style. The theatre can be used together with our drama room to create an even larger space or to provide break-out space.
There is a stage, projector, full PA system, lighting, lectern and a grand piano.
Classrooms
Our classrooms are perfect as training spaces, break-out rooms or to host meetings. The smallest classroom measures 7.7m x 7.1m while our largest classrooms measure 8.1m x 7.3m.
All classrooms have interactive smart boards.
Café Area
The café area is located on the ground floor with easy access to the other facilities. It has a modern feel and would be suitable for a break-out area, lunch or dinner party. It seats 140 people.
This space is also suitable for a reception/registration area.
Rooftop Terrace
A million pound view in Chelsea for a fraction of the price?
Book our rooftop terrace in combination with our theatre to use as a break out space or a champagne reception and wow your guests with a 360-degree view across London.

pageCache.pageTitle: CHELSEA ACADEMY CELEBRATES FANTASTIC GCSE RESULTS - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text:
We are delighted to share and celebrate our 2026 GCSE results with strong improvements on our 2025 results. 57% of all grades in Maths & English were 9-5 and our overall outcomes will place us in the top 20% of schools nationally! Congratulations to all our hard working Year 11s, many of whom have now enrolled into our Sixth Form.
Some fantastic individual success stories with the following students being awarded these top grades:
Nikita – 6 x Grade 9; 3 x Grade 8
Kareem – 6 x Grade 9; 5 x Grade 8
Bahman – 6 x Grade 9, 1 x Grade 8 & 3 x Grade 7
Salim – 5 x Grade 9; 3 x Grade 8
Charlie – 3 x Grade 9, 5 x Grade 8 & 2 x Grade 7
Scarlett – 1 x Grade 9, 3 x Grade 8 & 4 x Grade 7
Mayar – 6 x Grade 8; 3 x Grade 7
Sophia – 3 x Grade 8; 4 x Grade 7

pageCache.pageTitle: Chelsea Academy Hosts Community Tea Party with Age UK - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text: We hosted our annual summer Community Tea Party in the Library last week in partnership with Age UK. It was fantastic to see so many guests and students enjoying conversations, fun and games and of course a delicious afternoon tea! Highlights were a multi-generational quiz in student/ guest teams, a round of bingo (with a generous £20 voucher as first prize donated by Juliet’s Cafe), and some wonderful musical performances from students. A big thank you to all – staff and students – who helped to make this such a special event.

pageCache.pageTitle: Radio 4 records at Chelsea Academy - Chelsea Academy
pageCache.text: We were delighted to host Radio 4’s Kitchen Cabinet earlier this week. The recording took place in our theatre and a panel of food writers, chefs and a food historian took food related questions from the audience. The programme- the last in the present series – is due to be aired on Radio 4 on 8 August.
